title: Trace anchoring and failure bucketization for inference pipelines
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build an end-to-end observability surface that reliably maps runtime failures to clear operational buckets (timeouts, overload, model runtime errors, protocol errors like HTTP/gRPC codes) and surfaces them in new dashboards. This includes: 1) trace anchoring: deterministic trace/span propagation from Edge -> Router -> Batch worker -> Model runtime -> Response path; 2) a failure bucketization pipeline that materializes a canonical failure_reason tag for each request; 3) dashboard surfaces and runbook links for SRE/Eng. The output will power SLO alerting, customer impact triage, and postmortem classification.
acceptance_criteria: Trace ID propagated and visible end-to-end for >=95% of sampled requests across hosted and Dedicated paths
Streaming enrichment job assigns canonical failure_reason for >=90% of error responses in the test namespace (rules + heuristics)
New dashboard panels: call-path waterfall, failure_reason distribution, 95/99 latency by failure_reason, and batch-size correlation are live in Console observability space
Incident runbook snippets linked from dashboard entries and included in the ops playbook doc
No customer-facing behavior changed; tracing headers are optional and sampled to keep cost under budget
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff with runtime, router, and observability leads. Agreed on trace semantics (use W3C traceparent as primary, fallback to X-Request-Id). Decided to add a short trace propagation shim in our fronting proxies to ensure compatibility with older clients.

2026-03-05: Prototype: added span tags for batch_size, kv_cache_hit, model_variant, and model_error_code in the serving runtime. Local end-to-end trace verified in staging using jaeger collector (https://staging-jaeger.internal.redwood).

2026-03-07: Data pipeline design review with Analytics. Chosen approach: Fluent Bit -> Kafka -> Flink enrichment job that applies deterministic rules first (timeout, 429, 503 overload signals, model OOM, decode errors), then writes canonical failure_reason to metrics topic. Rationale: low-latency enrichment and easier schema evolution vs. batch ETL.

2026-03-10: UX/PM review. PM requested a compact failure_reason drilldown widget and a timeline view showing model fallback events. Design suggested color palette and accessibility constraints for high-severity buckets.

2026-03-12: Started implementation of Flink enrichment job in infra repo. Plumbed OTLP -> kafka exporter for spans. Working on consistent span attribute names across repos. First integration test failing due to missing traceparent in legacy internal load balancer (LB-legacy).
blockers: LB-legacy does not forward W3C traceparent header; need infra change or shim. Affects Dedicated/private customers behind that LB.
Telemetry cost approval: increased sampling and Kafka throughput will change observability spend; finance signoff required before full rollout.
notes: Classification approach: initial deterministic rules prioritized for precision (timeouts detected by span end/time delta or 504 HTTP/gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), then a small tuned ML model (post-rollout) will handle ambiguous cases like 'slow decode vs model stall'.

Edge cases: content filtering and policy rejections are classified separately as 'policy_reject' to avoid masking runtime errors; model return codes will be mapped to model_error subclasses (OOM, nan/inf, tokenizer_error).
Operational play: dashboards should link to a lightweight pre-filled PagerDuty responder list with correct escalation for customer-impacting buckets (high).
